episodes.title: Season 1: How and Why We Read
episodes.description: Explore why people read, what critical reading involves, and how literature helps people communicate.

episodes.title: Season 1: Of Pentameter & Bear Baiting – Romeo & Juliet Part 1
episodes.description: In which John Green examines Romeo & Juliet by William Shakespeare.

episodes.title: Season 1: Love or Lust? Romeo & Juliet Part 2
episodes.description: Examine love, lust, and social obligations in Romeo and Juliet and how Verona’s conventions contribute to the lovers’ downfall.

episodes.title: Season 1: Like Pale Gold – The Great Gatsby, Part 1
episodes.description: In which John Green explores F. Scott Fitzgerald's novel of the Jazz Age, The Great Gatsby.

episodes.title: Season 1: Was Gatsby Great? The Great Gatsby Part 2
episodes.description: Examine Gatsby’s pursuit of Daisy, his moral character, and Fitzgerald’s use of time, poetic language, and irony.

episodes.title: Season 1: Language, Voice, and Holden Caulfield – The Catcher in the Rye, Part 1
episodes.description: In which John Green examines JD Salinger's novel The Catcher in the Rye.

episodes.title: Season 1: Holden, JD, and the Red Cap – The Catcher in the Rye, Part 2
episodes.description: Explore how Salinger’s wartime experiences, education, and relationships inform Holden Caulfield in The Catcher in the Rye.

episodes.title: Season 1: Before I Got My Eye Put Out – The Poetry of Emily Dickinson
episodes.description: Explore Emily Dickinson’s poetic language, structure, unusual punctuation, and enduring relevance.

episodes.title: Season 2: A Long and Difficult Journey, or The Odyssey
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about Homer's Odyssey.

episodes.title: Season 2: Fate, Family, and Oedipus Rex
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about one of the least family-friendly family dramas in the history of family dramas, Oedipus Rex.

episodes.title: Season 2: Ghosts, Murder, and More Murder – Hamlet, Part 1
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about Hamlet, William Shakespeare's longest and most-performed play.

episodes.title: Season 2: Ophelia, Gertrude, and Regicide – Hamlet, Part 2
episodes.description: Examine gender, power, and agency in Hamlet through Ophelia and Gertrude, alongside regicide and Hamlet’s motivations.

episodes.title: Season 2: Don’t Reanimate Corpses! Frankenstein, Part 1
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about Mary Shelley's novel, Frankenstein.

episodes.title: Season 2: Frankenstein, Part 2
episodes.description: Compare critical interpretations of Frankenstein, Victor’s motivations, Romanticism, and the moral limits of science.

episodes.title: Season 2: Reader, it’s Jane Eyre
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about Charlotte Brontë's classic coming-of-age novel, Jane Eyre.

episodes.title: Season 2: If One Finger Brought Oil – Things Fall Apart, Part 1
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about Chinua Achebe's 1958 novel, Things Fall Apart.

episodes.title: Season 2: Things Fall Apart, Part 2
episodes.description: Explore the colonial and decolonial contexts of Things Fall Apart, Achebe’s upbringing, and Okonkwo’s fate.

episodes.title: Season 2: To Kill a Mockingbird, Part 1
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about Harper Lee's famous novel, To Kill a Mockingbird.

episodes.title: Season 2: Race, Class, and Gender in To Kill a Mockingbird
episodes.description: Examine race, class, and gender in To Kill a Mockingbird through Scout’s encounters with her community and the trial of Tom Robinson.

episodes.title: Season 2: Aliens, Time Travel, and Dresden – Slaughterhouse-Five Part I
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about Kurt Vonnegut's most famous novel, Slaughterhouse-Five.

episodes.title: Season 2: PTSD and Alien Abduction – Slaughterhouse-Five Part 2
episodes.description: In which John Green continues to teach you about Slaughterhouse-Five by Kurt Vonnegut as an anti-war novel, and what exactly anti-war novels are good for.

episodes.title: Season 2: Slavery, Ghosts, and Beloved
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about Beloved by Toni Morrison.

episodes.title: Season 2: Langston Hughes & the Harlem Renaissance
episodes.description: John will teach you a bit about Hughes's background, and he'll examine a few of his best-known poems.

episodes.title: Season 2: The Poetry of Sylvia Plath
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about the poetry of Sylvia Plath.

episodes.title: Season 3: Their Eyes Were Watching God
episodes.description: Explore Zora Neale Hurston’s life and how interpretations of Their Eyes Were Watching God have changed.

episodes.title: Season 3: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn Part 1
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about Mark Twain's The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn.

episodes.title: Season 3: The Raft, the River, and The Weird Ending of Huckleberry Finn
episodes.description: Explore the island, river, and raft as metaphors in Huckleberry Finn and consider criticism of the novel’s ending.

episodes.title: Season 3: Shakespeare’s Sonnets
episodes.description: We're learning about sonnets, and English Literature's best-known purveyor of those fourteen-line paeans, William Shakespeare.

episodes.title: Season 3: Lord of the Flies
episodes.description: John is talking about one of his least favorite novels, Lord of the Flies by William Golding.

episodes.title: Season 3: 100 Years of Solitude Part 1
episodes.description: Explore the Buendía family and the representation of time in Gabriel García Márquez’s One Hundred Years of Solitude.

episodes.title: Season 3: 100 Years of Solitude Part 2
episodes.description: Continue examining Gabriel García Márquez’s One Hundred Years of Solitude.

episodes.title: Season 3: Invisible Man
episodes.description: We’re on to reading Ralph Ellison’s great novel about the black experience in America after World War II, Invisible Man.

episodes.title: Season 3: Sula
episodes.description: John is talking about Toni Morrison's novel of friendship, betrayal, and loss, Sula.

episodes.title: Season 4: 1984 by George Orwell, Part 1
episodes.description: Explore Orwell’s Nineteen Eighty-Four through surveillance, government power, and the use of language by repressive regimes.

episodes.title: Season 4: George Orwell’s 1984, Part 2
episodes.description: Explore surveillance and the possibility of controlling thought through language in Orwell’s Nineteen Eighty-Four.

episodes.title: Season 4: The Handmaid’s Tale, Part 1
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about Margaret Atwood's speculative fiction novel, The Handmaid's Tale.

episodes.title: Season 4: The Handmaid’s Tale, Part 2
episodes.description: Examine narrative perspective and gender in The Handmaid’s Tale, including its final chapter’s male scholarly viewpoint.

episodes.title: Season 4: Candide
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Literature, John Green teaches you about Voltaire's hugely important Enlightenment novel, Candide.

episodes.title: Season 4: The Parable of the Sower
episodes.description: John is teaching you about the near-future dystopia in Octavia Butler's Parable of the Sower.

episodes.title: Season 4: The Yellow Wallpaper
episodes.description: Today on Crash Course Literature, John Green teaches you about "The Yellow Wallpaper," a short story by Charlotte Perkins Gilman.

episodes.title: Season 4: To the Lighthouse
episodes.description: John Green teaches you about Virginia Woolf's modernist novel, To the Lighthouse.

episodes.title: Season 4: Free Will, Witches, Murder, and Macbeth, Part 1
episodes.description: Examine free will and predestination in Macbeth and ask whether the protagonist’s violent choices were inevitable.

episodes.title: Season 4: Gender, Guilt, and Fate – Macbeth, Part 2
episodes.description: Examine gender, character, and Macbeth’s role as an early antihero in Shakespeare’s tragedy.

episodes.title: Season 4: Pride and Prejudice, Part 1
episodes.description: Explore Jane Austen’s life, Regency England, and the network of relationships in Pride and Prejudice.

episodes.title: Season 4: Liberals, Conservatives, and Pride and Prejudice, Part 2
episodes.description: Examine materialism, competing political interpretations, and the tension between personal happiness and family obligations in Pride and Prejudice.
